text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A municipal records office files inspection reports, payment receipts, and correspondence in a centralized document management system. Each record carries a unique identifier, filing date, assigned officer, and status field. Standard workflow requires digital upload, digital signature, and retention in both the primary register and a read-only archival mirror.

2) What occurred: The actor accessed the digital document management system under a named account holding inspector privileges. The actor retrieved a dated inspection report referencing a residential address, a code classification, and a non-compliant status. The actor opened the record editor and modified the status field from a value indicating violation to a value indicating compliance. The actor replaced the primary report document with an altered copy containing modified findings and a revised signature block. The actor entered a payment transaction into the financial ledger system, recording a remittance from a named account to a designated fund, and linked the transaction to the inspection identifier. The actor transmitted the altered document file via a personal email channel to a secondary recipient. The actor deleted two draft versions of the report from the system trash and edited the audit log entry timestamps associated with the session.

3) Materials/access observed: Access was exercised through a privileged user account on the internal network. The materials involved included a dated inspection report document, a financial ledger entry, two email message objects, and system audit log records. The actor possessed read and write permissions to the document store, the ledger module, and the log viewer.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The inspection report document hash differs from the archival mirror copy. The status field change lacks an associated justification memo. The financial ledger entry shows a manual input flag and an account number not associated with standard municipal vendor lists. Two email message objects show a sender address outside the municipal domain and a file attachment matching the altered document hash. The audit log contains sequential entries with timestamp gaps, and the trash bin history was purged during the same session window as the record modification.
